source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
To get good yields, farmers should select land based on soil type and drainage. Suitable soils for watermelon include sandy loam, reddish (laterite-influenced) loam, and light sandy soils — soils that drain water quickly and do not stay waterlogged. Recommended soil pH is around 5.8 to 6.8. Heavy clay soil and land that holds standing water for long periods after rain or irrigation should be avoided, since it damages the watermelon's root system and encourages root and vine diseases.

Before planting, the field should be plowed at least two times, including a cross-plowing pass, so the soil is well broken up and loosened. Well-tilled soil allows better air circulation to the roots, helps the crop establish and grow faster, and helps the soil retain moisture better for the crop. Plowing also helps destroy weeds, insect pests, and disease organisms that may be present in the soil before planting.
